boards.school_name: The University of Texas at San Antonio
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Main Campus places for collaborative study, low-key breaks, recreation, and campus cultural life.

cards.title: Sombrilla Plaza
cards.subtitle: Main Campus central plaza
cards.notes: Use the plaza as a visible meet-up point before campus events, then check posted programming for organization tables, games, or other activities.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor setting that also hosts student-organization programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA reported that Día en la Sombrilla is held in Sombrilla Plaza and features student organizations hosting games and selling treats for fundraising.
cards.source_title: Viva Fiesta! Where to spot a Roadrunner during San Antonio’s favorite time of the year
cards.access_notes: Outdoor event programming varies; consult UTSA event information before planning around a specific activity.

cards.title: JPL Quiet Study
cards.subtitle: John Peace Library, second floor
cards.notes: Bring a focused task and use the designated quiet area when you need independent work without reserving a group room.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study option inside the John Peace Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA Libraries lists Quiet Study in room JPL 2.01.34 among its available quiet study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located in JPL 2.01.34; follow library guidance and current building access policies.

cards.title: GroupSpot
cards.subtitle: John Peace Library, second floor near the Information Desk
cards.notes: Meet project partners near the Information Desk and use this designated collaborative area to organize work before booking a room if needed.
cards.short_summary: A named JPL space intended for group-project work.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA Libraries identifies GroupSpot on JPL's second floor near the Information Desk as a space for working on group projects.
cards.access_notes: Find it on JPL's second floor near the Information Desk; availability depends on library operations.

cards.title: JPL Third Floor Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: John Peace Library, third floor
cards.notes: Choose the third floor when your group needs refreshed collaborative space; coordinate first and shift to a reservable room for a longer session.
cards.short_summary: A renovated library floor with student-focused study rooms and collaborative areas.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA Libraries states that the reopened JPL third floor includes new furniture, study rooms, and collaborative spaces.
cards.source_title: UTSA Libraries opens JPL third floor with goals for the future
cards.access_notes: Inside the John Peace Library; library access and room availability can change by term or day.

cards.title: Roost Gameroom
cards.subtitle: H-E-B UTSA Student Union, second floor
cards.notes: Use a break between classes for a board game, table game, or console session, and confirm the posted schedule before walking over.
cards.short_summary: A student gameroom with table games, board games, and multiple consoles.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA says the Roost Gameroom is open to all UTSA students and offers pool, air hockey, foosball, ping pong, board games, and gaming systems.
cards.access_notes: On the second floor of the H-E-B UTSA Student Union; the official page posts seasonal hours.

cards.title: Fountain Courtyard
cards.subtitle: H-E-B UTSA Student Union, first floor
cards.notes: Use this named Student Union courtyard as an easy indoor-adjacent place to regroup before heading to nearby services, food, or events.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed courtyard within the first-floor Student Union layout.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA's Student Union building map lists Fountain Courtyard on the first floor alongside campus services, dining, and meeting spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located on the Student Union first floor; observe posted event setups and building rules.

cards.title: Window Lounge
cards.subtitle: H-E-B UTSA Student Union, first floor
cards.notes: Pick the Window Lounge for a short conversation or a pause between Student Union errands, keeping shared seating available for others.
cards.short_summary: A named lounge shown on the Student Union's first-floor map.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA's Student Union building map lists Window Lounge on the first floor.
cards.access_notes: Located on the Student Union first floor; seating and access may be affected by events.

cards.title: UTSA Main Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Art Building, room 2.03.04, Main Campus
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition listing, then build in time to look closely and discuss the work after your visit without needing a ticket.
cards.short_summary: A Main Campus gallery presenting curated and juried art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA identifies the Main Art Gallery in the Art Building, room 2.03.04, and states that all gallery exhibitions are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: In the Art Building on Main Campus; confirm current exhibition dates and gallery hours before visiting.

cards.title: Climbing Center
cards.subtitle: Recreation and Wellness Center
cards.notes: Try a staff-supported introductory climb if you are new, or complete the required orientation and skills check before planning independent climbing.
cards.short_summary: UTSA's campus climbing wall supports introductory climbs, orientations, and clinics.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA Campus Recreation says its Recreation and Wellness Center climbing wall reaches 54 feet and offers Try-It Climbs, belay orientations, skills checks, and clinics.
cards.access_notes: Located in the Recreation and Wellness Center; check facility hours and complete required orientations before climbing independently.

cards.title: Rec Field Complex
cards.subtitle: Near Lot 12 and Sam Barshop Boulevard
cards.notes: Bring a group for open recreation when fields are available, and use the field house checkout rather than assuming personal equipment is required.
cards.short_summary: A lighted turf complex used for club sports, intramurals, and daily open recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA says the Rec Field Complex has soccer, football, and multipurpose turf fields; club and intramural programs use it, with open recreation available daily.
cards.access_notes: Near Lot 12 and Sam Barshop Boulevard; verify field availability and weather status before arriving.

boards.school_name: The University of Texas at San Antonio
boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented, under-21-safe art and history outings with free admission or free access for UTSA students and local visitors.

cards.title: See an exhibition at UTSA Main Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Arts Building, UTSA Main Campus
cards.notes: Meet in the Arts Building and take in the current exhibition together. Check the gallery calendar first because the space closes between shows.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery visit with publicly accessible exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA states that all exhibitions at its galleries are free and open to the public; the Main Art Gallery is in the Art Building on Main Campus.
cards.access_notes: Public gallery; current listed hours are Thursday 10 a.m.–2 p.m. and Friday–Saturday 10 a.m.–3 p.m. Confirm exhibitions before going.

cards.title: Browse the Russell Hill Rogers Galleries
cards.subtitle: UTSA Southwest Campus, 1201 Navarro
cards.notes: Plan a downtown art stop with a friend and walk through the current installation. The galleries are inside the Santikos Building on UTSA’s Southwest Campus.
cards.short_summary: Free UTSA exhibitions in a downtown campus setting.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA states that all exhibitions are free and open to the public and identifies the Russell Hill Rogers Galleries at its Southwest Campus.
cards.access_notes: Public gallery; listed hours are Thursday–Saturday, noon–5 p.m., plus appointments. Check for exhibition gaps or holiday closures.

cards.title: Walk through Artpace exhibitions
cards.subtitle: 445 North Main Avenue, downtown San Antonio
cards.notes: Use Artpace as a no-cost conversation stop: look through the galleries, then compare one work each that held your attention before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A free downtown contemporary-art visit.
cards.evidence_claim: Artpace describes itself as free and open to the public and lists its location at 445 North Main Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Public visiting hours listed: Monday–Friday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday noon–5 p.m. Exhibitions and programs may vary.

cards.title: Visit Ruby City’s contemporary art spaces
cards.subtitle: 150 Camp Street, downtown San Antonio
cards.notes: Drop in to view the exhibitions, then spend a few minutes outside in Chris Park. Keep the plan simple: no advance booking is needed for standard visits.
cards.short_summary: Free contemporary art and outdoor space near downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruby City says admission is free, visitors need no advance booking for the site or exhibitions, and its public spaces include Ruby City and Chris Park.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; Ruby City is listed Thursday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m., while Chris Park is listed Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–6 p.m.

cards.title: Explore Contemporary at Blue Star
cards.subtitle: 116 Blue Star, Blue Star Arts Complex
cards.notes: Choose an exhibition day and give yourselves time to read the wall text, then use the Art Learning Lab prompts to start a low-key art conversation.
cards.short_summary: Free contemporary-art exhibitions in the Blue Star Arts Complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Contemporary at Blue Star states that admission to its exhibitions and programs is free and identifies its location in Building C of the Blue Star Arts Complex.
cards.source_title: Visit the Contemporary at Blue Star
cards.access_notes: Public exhibition hours are listed Wednesday noon–5 p.m., Thursday–Friday noon–8 p.m., Saturday–Sunday 10 a.m.–6 p.m.; confirm installation closures.

cards.title: Use your UTSA ID at SAMA
cards.subtitle: 200 West Jones Avenue, downtown San Antonio
cards.notes: Bring your current UTSA ID for a self-guided museum visit. Pick one gallery to explore together rather than trying to cover the whole collection at once.
cards.short_summary: UTSA community members receive free general admission with ID.
cards.evidence_claim: The San Antonio Museum of Art lists UTSA students, faculty, and staff among university partners who receive free general admission with school IDs.
cards.source_title: Visit | San Antonio Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Bring a UTSA school ID. Free general admission does not necessarily cover special-exhibition surcharges; the museum lists Tuesday hours through 7 p.m.

cards.title: Schedule a Free Tuesday at the Witte
cards.subtitle: 3801 Broadway, San Antonio
cards.notes: If you are a Bexar County resident, meet during the museum’s Tuesday free-admission window and focus your visit on one exhibit or the outdoor grounds.
cards.short_summary: A weekly no-cost museum window for Bexar County residents.
cards.evidence_claim: The Witte Museum states that Bexar County residents receive free general admission every Tuesday from 3 to 6 p.m.
cards.source_title: Free Tuesday for Bexar County Residents | Witte Museum
cards.access_notes: Free general admission is for Bexar County residents on Tuesdays, 3–6 p.m.; bring any documentation the museum requests and review current exhibit policies.

cards.title: Catch a free Thursday evening at the McNay
cards.subtitle: 6000 North New Braunfels Avenue, San Antonio
cards.notes: Plan for Thursday after class and visit the main collection galleries together. Optional featured exhibitions can carry a separate charge, so stay with the free galleries.
cards.short_summary: Free main-collection access on Thursday evenings.
cards.evidence_claim: The McNay visitor guide lists free Thursday nights from 4 to 9 p.m. and free first Sundays for the main collection galleries.
cards.access_notes: Free Thursday nights are listed 4–9 p.m. for main collection galleries. Featured exhibitions may have an optional additional charge.

cards.title: Join the Mission San José ranger-guided walk
cards.subtitle: Mission San José Visitor Center, San Antonio Missions National Historical Park
cards.notes: Arrive before the daily walk at the visitor center and follow the paved route with a friend. Bring water and respect the historic structures and marked paths.
cards.short_summary: A free, ranger-led introduction to Mission San José.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists free daily ranger-guided walks at Mission San José at 10 a.m. and 11 a.m.; all park programs are free of charge.
cards.source_title: Guided Programs | San Antonio Missions National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Walks begin at the Mission San José Visitor Center, are first-come first-served, weather permitting, and limited to 50 people. No ranger programs on first Wednesdays.

cards.title: Meet a ranger at Mission Concepción
cards.subtitle: Mission Concepción, San Antonio Missions National Historical Park
cards.notes: Make Mission Concepción a daytime history outing and join the listed daily ranger program. Use the visit as a slow walk-and-talk, not a rush through the site.
cards.short_summary: A free daily ranger program at one of the park’s four mission sites.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service lists a daily 10 a.m. ranger program at Mission Concepción and states that all park programs are free of charge.
cards.source_title: Guided Programs | San Antonio Missions National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Mission Concepción’s ranger program is listed daily at 10 a.m., weather permitting. The National Park Service says all programs are free; check updates before travel.

cards.title: Lark San Antonio: Runner Route 45/47
cards.subtitle: Chase Hill Boulevard corridor near UTSA
cards.notes: Check UTSA’s Route 45 or 47 listing for the Campus Oval connection, then confirm the current Runner timetable before departing.
cards.short_summary: A named Chase Hill Boulevard-area destination on the Campus Oval route.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA lists Lark San Antonio as served by Routes 45 and 47 to and from the Campus Oval.
cards.access_notes: UTSA identifies this destination on Routes 45 and 47; review the current Runner schedule before travel.

boards.school_name: The University of Texas at San Antonio
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UT San Antonio rituals, symbols, ceremonies, and campus legends tied to Roadrunner identity.

cards.title: Answer “Birds Up!” with the Roadrunner sign
cards.subtitle: UT San Antonio spirit greeting
cards.notes: Hold your palm outward, curl the first three fingers inward, and leave thumb and pinky raised when sharing a Roadrunner greeting.
cards.short_summary: The thumb forms the roadrunner’s head and the pinky its tail.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio documents the Roadrunner hand sign as a spirit gesture used when someone says “Birds Up!” and gives its hand-position instructions.
cards.access_notes: Use as a school-spirit greeting at games, events, or in passing.

cards.title: Save the Sombrilla Fountain touch for finals
cards.subtitle: Sombrilla Fountain, Main Campus
cards.notes: During finals week, visit the Sombrilla Fountain and touch its wall if you want to take part in the campus good-luck legend.
cards.short_summary: The same legend warns against touching the wall at other times of year.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio identifies the Sombrilla Fountain as the Fountain of Luck and says campus legend connects touching its wall during finals week with exam luck.
cards.access_notes: Campus legend; participate only by touching the fountain wall during finals week.

cards.title: Look for the 31 bronze Milagros hearts
cards.subtitle: Downtown Campus building facades
cards.notes: Walk the Downtown Campus and look closely at building facades for Diana Rodriguez Gil’s bronze hearts; the tradition is to rub one for a miracle.
cards.short_summary: The scattered hearts turn a public-art search into a campus ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio says 31 bronze hearts from alumna Diana Rodriguez Gil’s Milagros project are on Downtown Campus facades and that tradition holds students rub a heart for a miracle.
cards.access_notes: View the artwork from publicly accessible campus areas; do not climb or damage building surfaces.

cards.title: Know Rowdy’s unusually theatrical debut
cards.subtitle: UT San Antonio mascot tradition
cards.notes: Spot Rowdy at university spirit occasions and remember the mascot first appeared by hatching from an egg at a 1981 basketball pep rally.
cards.short_summary: The mascot’s debut followed the Roadrunner’s official 1977 selection.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio reports that the Roadrunner became its official mascot on December 12, 1977, and that the first costumed mascot debuted by hatching from an egg at a 1981 basketball pep rally.
cards.access_notes: Observe the mascot at scheduled university events.

cards.entity_name: UT San Antonio Class Ring Overnight at the Alamo
cards.title: Follow the rings’ overnight trip to the Alamo
cards.subtitle: Class-ring ceremony tradition
cards.notes: If participating in a ring ceremony, look for the Alumni Association’s delivery of rings after their documented overnight stay at the Alamo.
cards.short_summary: Every UT San Antonio class ring has made the overnight stay since 2012.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio states that every UT San Antonio class ring has stayed overnight at the Alamo the night before the ring ceremony since 2012 and is hand-delivered by the Alumni Association.
cards.access_notes: Ring purchase and ceremony participation are separate from this documented tradition.

cards.title: Find the iron Rowdy overlooking campus
cards.subtitle: Main Campus landmark
cards.notes: Pause at the Rowdy Statue to see the campus-scale mascot sculpture created by R. G. Box after the student-led Bring Rowdy Home campaign.
cards.short_summary: The 2013 sculpture is six feet tall, 11 feet long, and weighs 1,000 pounds.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio says the Rowdy Statue arrived in September 2013, was funded through the student-led Bring Rowdy Home campaign, and was created by Raymond George Box.
cards.access_notes: View and photograph from the surrounding campus area; do not climb the sculpture.

cards.title: Mark Fiesta with Día En La Sombrilla
cards.subtitle: Sombrilla Plaza, Main Campus
cards.notes: Check the university calendar during Fiesta season, then join the daylong Sombrilla Plaza fair for its documented music, medals, food, and cascarones.
cards.short_summary: UT San Antonio’s campus Fiesta event is rooted in San Antonio’s spring celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio describes Día En La Sombrilla as a daylong fair in Sombrilla Plaza with food, music, medals, and cascarones during Fiesta.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current event schedule and any attendance details with UT San Antonio before going.

cards.title: Make room for Homecoming’s Best Fest
cards.subtitle: Annual UT San Antonio Homecoming week
cards.notes: During Homecoming week, check the program for Best Fest, Spirit of the Roadrunner recognition, and the football game’s related activities.
cards.short_summary: Homecoming began in 1985 to connect students and alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio says Homecoming began in 1985 and identifies Best Fest, Spirit of the Roadrunner awards, and the Homecoming football game as weeklong highlights.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current Homecoming schedule and requirements with UT San Antonio.

cards.title: Learn the “Go, Roadrunners, Go!” refrain
cards.subtitle: UT San Antonio battle song
cards.notes: Follow the official fight-song text before a spirit event so you can recognize the repeated “Go, Roadrunners, Go!” and “Fight, Roadrunners, Fight!” lines.
cards.short_summary: The song names UTSA’s blue, orange, and white school colors.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio publishes the UT San Antonio Fight Song, including its “Go, Roadrunners, Go!” and “Fight, Roadrunners, Fight!” refrains.
cards.access_notes: Use the official text and audio on the university traditions page for reference.

cards.title: Listen for the commencement mariachi serenade
cards.subtitle: UT San Antonio commencement tradition
cards.notes: At commencement, stay through the closing celebration to experience the mariachi performance that UT San Antonio connects to its San Antonio setting.
cards.short_summary: Mariachis have performed at UT San Antonio graduation celebrations since its first 1974 ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio states that mariachis have performed at its graduation celebrations since the university’s first graduation in August 1974.
cards.access_notes: Commencement attendance is governed by the university’s current ceremony and guest procedures.

boards.school_name: The University of Texas at San Antonio
boards.title: Your First Weekend at The University of Texas at San Antonio, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A campus-first, under-21-safe sequence for learning UT San Antonio landmarks and traditions over a first weekend.

cards.title: Begin at John Peace Library
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Main Campus
cards.notes: Start at the Main Campus library, locate the front desk, and use the floor maps to pick a study spot or identify academic-support services for a later visit.
cards.short_summary: A practical first landmark with study space and campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA Libraries identifies the John Peace Library as located on the Main Campus and provides floor maps and building information.
cards.access_notes: Consult UTSA Libraries for current building access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Find the Sombrilla Fountain
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Sombrilla Plaza, Main Campus
cards.notes: Walk to the fountain outside the library and use the plaza as an orientation point. Take a photo from the walkway and leave the fountain structure undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A central Main Campus landmark and documented Roadrunner tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio describes the Sombrilla Fountain as an iconic Main Campus landmark in Sombrilla Plaza near the John Peace Library.
cards.source_title: Being a Roadrunner | UT San Antonio Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; observe posted rules and do not enter or climb on the fountain.

cards.title: Meet Rowdy at the Roadrunner Statue
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Central Plaza, Main Campus
cards.notes: Continue to Central Plaza for a photo with the iron Rowdy sculpture. Try the documented Birds Up pose, but keep both feet on the ground and do not climb it.
cards.short_summary: A named mascot sculpture near the Sombrilla.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio identifies the Roadrunner Statue in Central Plaza near the Sombrilla and advises visitors not to climb on it.
cards.source_title: Photo Locations | UT San Antonio Commencement
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public artwork; photograph it without climbing or touching the sculpture.

cards.title: Use the Student Union as your reset point
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Main Campus
cards.notes: Stop at the information desk and look over current campus services, programs, and building wayfinding. It is a useful place to regroup before continuing your walk.
cards.short_summary: A Main Campus hub for student services and wayfinding.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio orientation materials identify the Student Union Information Desk as a helpful Main Campus location.
cards.source_title: UT San Antonio In-Person Orientation Experience
cards.access_notes: Services and building access may vary; check current Student Union information before arrival.

cards.title: Plan an active stop at the Rec Center
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Main Campus
cards.notes: Visit the Recreation Wellness Center to learn its layout and plan a future workout or recreation session. Bring required identification and verify entry eligibility first.
cards.short_summary: UTSA’s named Main Campus recreation facility.
cards.evidence_claim: UTSA Campus Recreation identifies the Recreation Wellness Center as a Main Campus facility and gives its campus-map location.
cards.source_title: Recreation Wellness Center | UTSA Campus Recreation
cards.access_notes: Check current facility hours, eligibility, and check-in requirements with Campus Recreation.

cards.title: Walk out to the UTSA Monuments
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · UTSA Oval, Main Campus
cards.notes: Use the Oval as a daylight walking destination and photograph the UTSA Monuments from the path. This is a clear checkpoint near the Main Campus entrance.
cards.short_summary: Named monument letters at the Main Campus Oval.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio identifies the UTSA Monuments as located at the UTSA Oval near the Main Campus entrance from Loop 1604.
cards.source_title: Photo Locations | UT San Antonio Commencement
cards.access_notes: Outdoor landmark; use walkways and remain aware of campus traffic near the entrance.

cards.title: Cross the Bridge of Love
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · Arts and Flawn Sciences Buildings, Main Campus
cards.notes: Find the bridge connecting the Arts and Flawn Sciences Buildings, then take the documented campus-story walk across it with friends or a new roommate.
cards.short_summary: A named bridge tied to a documented UTSA campus legend.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio Student Affairs identifies the Bridge of Love as connecting the Arts and Flawn Sciences Buildings on the Main Campus.
cards.source_title: Being a Roadrunner | UT San Antonio Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Use the bridge normally and keep paths clear for people traveling between buildings.

cards.title: Learn the Birds Up hand sign
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · UT San Antonio tradition
cards.notes: Practice the official Roadrunner hand-sign instructions, then use it in a campus photo or when greeting fellow Roadrunners at an appropriate school event.
cards.short_summary: A documented UT San Antonio school-spirit gesture.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio documents the Roadrunner hand sign and explains how it is used to show school spirit.
cards.access_notes: Use the gesture respectfully; it does not require an event ticket or special equipment.

cards.title: Make a Downtown Campus stop at Bill Miller Plaza
cards.subtitle: Sunday morning · Downtown Campus
cards.notes: If you are traveling to the Downtown Campus, make Bill Miller Plaza your meeting point and use it to orient yourself before exploring public campus pathways.
cards.short_summary: The central green-space landmark on UTSA’s Downtown Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio identifies Bill Miller Plaza as the green space at the center of the Downtown Campus where pathways intersect.
cards.source_title: Navigating UTSA: Your road map to get around campus | UT San Antonio Today
cards.access_notes: Plan transportation before leaving Main Campus and follow current Downtown Campus access guidance.

cards.title: Look for the Milagros hearts
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · Downtown Campus
cards.notes: While on the Downtown Campus, look closely at building facades for the bronze hearts in the Milagros art project. Observe the artwork without rubbing or altering it.
cards.short_summary: A documented campus art project of 31 bronze hearts.
cards.evidence_claim: UT San Antonio documents Milagros as 31 bronze hearts sculpted by alumna Diana Rodriguez Gil on Downtown Campus building facades.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior artwork from public areas and follow all posted campus access rules.
